How much does Discogs take per sale?

Discogs charges sellers a 9% selling fee on the item price plus the shipping the buyer pays, with a $0.10 minimum and a $150 maximum per order. Listing is free. The rate rose from 8% to 9% on May 22, 2023. On top of that, payment processing comes out of each order. Discogs does not publish one processing rate for every seller, so the examples below use 2.9% + $0.30 as an assumption; replace it with the figure on your own payout statement in the calculator.

The formula

selling fee = 9% × (item price + buyer-paid shipping), limited to $0.10–$150

processing = rate × (item price + buyer-paid shipping) + flat fee

payout = item price + buyer-paid shipping − selling fee − processing − your own postage cost

Worked example 1: a $50 record, no buyer-paid shipping

LineAmount
Item price$50.00
Selling fee (9% of $50.00)$4.50
Processing (2.9% of $50.00 + $0.30)$1.75
Reaches you, before postage and cost$43.75

Worked example 2: the fee reaches shipping too

LineAmount
Item price$20.00
Buyer-paid shipping$6.00
Combined$26.00
Selling fee (9% of $26.00)$2.34
Processing (2.9% of $26.00 + $0.30)$1.05
Reaches you, before postage and cost$22.61

The selling fee is $2.34, not $1.80 (9% of the $20 item alone). Because the fee follows the total, moving money between the price and the shipping line changes nothing: what moves your profit is the total the buyer pays and what the label actually costs you.

Cheap records and grails are different problems. On a $3 single, the flat $0.30 is a tenth of the sale and the whole cut is about 22%. On a $2,500 record the $150 cap holds the selling fee to 6%. The calculator’s fee ladder shows both on your own postage and costs.

Price your own record in the Discogs fee calculator — it runs in your browser and uploads nothing.

Common questions

How much does Discogs take on a $50 record?

A 9% selling fee of $4.50, plus payment processing. At an assumed 2.9% + $0.30 processing that is $1.75 more, so about $43.75 reaches you before postage and what you paid for the record.

Does Discogs charge its fee on shipping?

Yes. The 9% applies to the item price plus the shipping the buyer pays. A $20 record with $6 shipping pays 9% of $26, which is $2.34, not 9% of $20.

What are the Discogs minimum and maximum fees?

The selling fee is at least $0.10 and at most $150 per order. The cap is reached at an order total of about $1,667.

No warranty. This page and the calculator are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. They are not legal, tax, financial, or selling advice. Verify every figure against your own Discogs payout statement. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Discogs; the name is used only to describe the published fee the tool computes against.

Discogs takes 9% of your shipping too.

Discogs charges a 9% selling fee on the item price plus the shipping the buyer pays (minimum $0.10, maximum $150 per order), and payment processing comes out on top. Put in a record, what you charged, what the postage cost you and what you paid for it, and see what lands in your account, the price that hits a profit target, and where on the price ladder the fixed fees stop mattering.

How much does Discogs take per sale?

The sale

Item price is what the buyer paid for the record(s). Buyer-paid shipping is what they paid you for postage. Postage you paid is what the label actually cost.

Discogs does not publish one processing rate for every seller, so the last two boxes start at 2.9% + $0.30 when blank. Copy the real figure from one of your own payout statements.

        Common questions

        How much does Discogs take per sale?

        A 9% selling fee, charged on the item price plus the shipping the buyer pays, with a $0.10 minimum and a $150 maximum per order, plus payment processing on top. A $50 record with no shipping pays $4.50 in selling fee; at an assumed 2.9% + $0.30 processing, about $1.75 more, so you keep about $43.75 before postage and what you paid for it.

        Does Discogs charge its fee on shipping?

        Yes. The 9% applies to the item price and the shipping together, so a $20 record with $6 shipping pays 9% of $26 ($2.34), not 9% of $20 ($1.80). Processing is charged on the same total. It makes no difference whether you raise the price or the shipping: the fee follows the total the buyer pays.

        What is the Discogs processing fee?

        It is separate from the 9% selling fee and is taken by the payment provider on the same order. Discogs does not publish a single rate for every seller, and third-party guides disagree (figures such as 2.7% + $0.25, 2.9% + $0.30 and 3.49% + $0.49 all circulate). This calculator starts at 2.9% + $0.30 and lets you overwrite both numbers from your own payout statement.

        Is there a maximum Discogs fee?

        Yes. Discogs caps the selling fee at $150 per order, which is reached at an order total of about $1,667. Above that the selling fee stops growing, though processing still applies to the whole order. There is also a $0.10 minimum.

        Is my data uploaded anywhere?

        No. Parsing and arithmetic happen entirely in your browser. Prices, costs, and payouts are never uploaded. If you use the save button, your numbers are written to this browser’s own local storage on this device only, and the forget button deletes them. The Copy shareable link button puts the same numbers in the page’s URL fragment, which your browser never sends to a server. The optional usage counter records only which features were used and the day, never any of your numbers.

vs-doing-the-fee-math-yourself.html.text:
← Back to the Discogs fee calculator

The Discogs fee calculator vs. doing the fee maths yourself

Most Discogs sellers price a record with a rule of thumb: take off about 10% and call it done. It is close for a mid-priced record sold with free shipping and wrong in four places the calculator handles.

QuestionRule of thumbCalculator
Is shipping in the fee base?Often forgottenYes, selling fee and processing both
Flat per-order processingIgnoredSeparate input
$150 cap on big salesOverpays the fee in your headApplied
Price for a target profitTrial and errorSolved, including across the cap
Fee at $3 vs $100 vs $2,500One numberFee ladder

Where a spreadsheet is fine

If you sell one kind of record at one price with one shipping rate, a spreadsheet with your own processing figure does the same thing. The calculator is for pricing a crate where the answer changes record by record, and for comparing Discogs against eBay, Etsy or Reverb on the same item through the where-to-sell calculator.

Open the Discogs fee calculator

Common questions

Why not just multiply by 0.91 in a spreadsheet?

Because the 9% is charged on item plus shipping, the processing has a flat per-order part, and the selling fee is capped at $150, so a flat percentage is wrong at both ends of your price range.

Do I need to know the Discogs processing rate?

It helps. Discogs does not publish one rate for every seller, so the calculator takes it as two boxes that start at 2.9% + $0.30. Copy your real figure from a payout statement and every result updates.
